newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - June 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - June 12.

text.p: This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company, which is responsible for its contents. -- BANK MUST ACCOUNT FOR INFLATION

UK chancellor Gordon Brown will make his annual Mansion House speech on Thursday, which will include a new system holding Eddie George, the governor of the Bank of England, responsible for any failure to meet inflation targets. It is expected the system will require George to write a formal letter to Brown each time the inflation rate is one percentage point above or below the inflation target rate of 2.5 per cent.
-- SANTER LOOKS TO SECURE EU DEAL ON JOBS

European Commission president Jacques Santer is seeking the authorisation of a jobs deal which will allow Lionel Jospin's French government to approve the Emu budget stability pact. Santer will hold talks with Jospin and President Jacques Chirac stressing that no negotiation can be made on the stability pact, but he will commit to a EU-wide pact which focuses on growth and job creation.
-- JOBS, WAGES FIGURES FUEL FEARS OF FRESH INFLATION

Fears that the UK will face another bout of inflation were heightened on Wednesday, as published figures showed a continued decline in unemployment and continuing high average earnings growth. Employment and education minister Andrew Smith commented that the figures were "consistent with a broad picture of rising output, growth in employment and falling unemployment".
-- PETROL PRICING TO BE PROBED BY OFT

The UK Office of Fair Trading (OFT) has appointed independent consultants from the National Economics Research Associates to begin an inquiry into petrol retailing, including an investigation into the effects of alleged predatory pricing by Esso through its Price-Watch programme. Independent oil suppliers have welcomed the move, declaring that their efforts to compete with the leading oil producers, who are able to sell oil below cost, are putting them out of business.
-- ENERGY GROUP CONSIDERS BID

Directors of Anglo-American company Energy Group will further consider a bid from U.S.-based utility PacifiCorp on Thursday, amid much speculation it will be accepted. Analysts have reacted favourably to the bid, saying it "makes excellent sense for shareholders", and the board at Energy Group is expected to make its decision by Friday at the earliest. The main concern at Energy Group is that PacifiCorp is able to secure financing for the deal before the terms of the transaction are announced.
-- MURDOCH TO SELL ASKY OPERATION TO CABLE RIVALS

Abandoning plans to expand his satellite television business into the U.S., media tycoon Rupert Murdoch has announced plans to take a "step back", and merge ASkyB with rival PrimeStar, a U.S.-based satellite operator. The deal involves Murdoch's News Corp taking a $1.1bn non-voting 30 per cent stake in PrimeStar, a consortium run by Time Warner, U.S. West, Cox Communications and Tele-Communications.
-- SOUR RESPONSE FROM MILK MARQUE CHIEF

UK dairy farmers marketing co-operative Milk Marque has seen its relation with Dairy Crest, Unigate and Northern Foods worsen after its chief executive David Yeomans stated the groups were uncompetitive and that if they could not meet EU standards for butter and milk powder sold into intervention "there must be something horribly wrong with their plant". Yeomans announced plans to write to the Office of Fair Trading suggesting an investigation into why the above companies refused to process Milk Marque's surplus milk.
-- TED BAKER SHIRTS TO GET 60 MLN STG TICKET

Fashion retailer and wholesaler Ted Baker is to arrive on the market this summer in an expected 20 million stg placing which could value it at between 55 million stg and 60 million stg. Ted Baker's founder, Ray Kelvin, who will become a millionaire from the deal, said he would use the listing to build a "global brand" rivalling labels such as Paul Smith and Hugo Boss. Kelvin currently owns about 70 per cent of the company, which should drop to 40 per cent after the float.
-- EXPRO EXPLOITS DEEP SEA FIELDS

John Dawson, chief executive of oilfield services group Expro International, has said the company plans to invest heavily into markets such as the Gulf of Mexico, fuelled by the increased development of deep water oilfields which is raising demand for advanced subsea equipment to complete wells. Expro has released figures for the year to the end of March, including increases in capital expenditure from 8.9 million stg to 14.9 million stg, pre-tax profits up 24 per cent to 17.8 million stg and turnover up 28 per cent to 105 million stg.
-- MANSFIELD TAKES WESTERN TRAIL

Mansfield Brewery has announced a 30 million stg package to be used to fuel expansion plans, by widening its themed pub range and moves into new parts of the UK. Managing director Bill McCosh said Mansfield was "open-minded" on acquiring another pub group. The expansion announcements follow a record performance for the group last year, with pre-tax profit up 13 per cent to 20.8 million stg on sales up eight per cent to 158.4 million stg.
